Rich people and broke people buy different kinds of things.

Kevin Trudeau explains what he calls the magic phrase: rich people buy appreciating assets, things that go up in value over time. Broke people buy things that go down in value over time.

A car, he says, is a depreciating asset. It is still an asset because you can sell it, but its value drops, most of all in the first three years.

What have you bought that lost value the longer you owned it?
